title: Gemini Tools and Application-Controlled Agent Loops
summary: This intermediate module teaches you to distinguish a Gemini function call from function execution and to manage the resulting application-controlled loop. After completing it, you can trace when an application should execute a function, return its result, continue the loop, or stop.
objectives: Explain the difference between a function declaration, a function call, and a function response.
Trace the responsibilities of Gemini and the application through a function-calling loop.
Determine whether the application should execute a requested function, return its result, continue the loop, or stop.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The previous citation record pointed to content/modules/google-gemini-practice/gemini-tools-and-agent-loops.json, identified in the update request as an unregistered publisher that had never been verified. That citation was replaced with Google's official function-calling documentation.

The source change affects the module's attribution and its wording about execution responsibility. The corrected material states that Gemini can request a function call, while the application is responsible for deciding whether to execute the function and for returning the resulting information. The learning scope remains tools and agent loops rather than expanding to unrelated Gemini features.

sections.title: Intermediate scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you can follow a request and response exchange and understand that an application can call an external function. It does not assume prior knowledge of a particular software library, programming language, version, or configuration format.

sections.title: Declaration, call, and response
paragraphs: A function declaration tells Gemini what an available function is intended to do and what information it accepts. It describes an application capability but does not implement or execute that capability.

A function call is a structured request produced by Gemini when it determines that the declared function may help answer the user's request. Producing the call does not mean that Gemini has executed the function.

The application receives the function call and decides whether to execute the corresponding function. If it does, the application sends the function result back as a function response so Gemini can use that information in a later response.
sections.callout: Keep the responsibility boundary explicit: Gemini requests a function call, and the application controls execution.

sections.title: Follow the application-controlled loop
paragraphs: The loop begins when the application supplies relevant function declarations together with the conversation. Gemini can then return either a response for the user or a function call.

When Gemini returns a function call, the application inspects the request and decides whether to execute the corresponding function. After execution, the application returns the function response to Gemini as part of the continuing conversation.

Gemini can use that returned information to produce a user-facing response. If it instead requests another function call, the application again controls whether that call is executed. The loop stops when the application receives a response that it will present to the user or when the application decides not to continue.

This sequence lets you diagnose responsibility at each step. A missing or incorrect function result is an application-side execution or integration issue, while a requested function call is model output that the application must still evaluate.

sections.title: Trace a conceptual example
paragraphs: Suppose an application declares a function that can retrieve information needed for a user's question. Gemini may respond with a function call containing the information required by that declaration.

The application inspects the call. If it chooses to execute the corresponding function, it collects the result and returns that result to Gemini as a function response. Gemini can then use the returned information to compose its next response.

At no point should the presence of a function call be treated as proof that the external action already occurred. The application remains the component that performs or declines the requested execution.

questions.prompt: What does a function declaration do in the workflow described by this module?
choices: It describes an available application function and the information it accepts.
It proves that the application has already executed the function.
It replaces the function result with a user-facing answer.
questions.explanation: A declaration describes an available capability. It does not implement the function or prove that execution occurred.

questions.prompt: Gemini returns a function call. Which component decides whether to execute the corresponding function?
choices: Gemini executes it automatically before returning the call.
The application inspects the call and decides whether to execute it.
The function declaration executes it without application involvement.
questions.explanation: The module identifies the application as the component that controls execution. A Gemini function call is a request, not proof of execution.

questions.prompt: After the application executes a requested function, what should it return to Gemini?
choices: A function response containing the function result
A claim that Gemini executed the function
questions.explanation: The application returns the result as a function response so Gemini can use the information in a later response.

questions.prompt: According to the module, when can the application-controlled loop stop?
choices: Only after Gemini requests the same function twice
When the application receives a response it will present to the user or decides not to continue
Immediately after supplying function declarations, before Gemini responds
questions.explanation: The loop can stop when there is a response the application will present or when the application decides not to continue.
